paper_metadata.title: Implementing Quantum Machine Learning in Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid quantum–classical fraud detection framework using a Variational Quantum Circuit and a classical neural network evaluated on the European credit card fraud dataset (284,807 transactions). On a simulator, the model reports recall 0.89, precision 0.82, F1-score 0.85, and AUC‑ROC 0.91 using a 70:30 train–test split. No direct experimental comparison with classical baselines or quantum hardware evaluation is provided.

experiments.description: Hybrid variational quantum-classical credit card fraud detection using a variational quantum circuit (VQC) with classical neural network post-processing on a simulated quantum environment.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) hybrid with classical neural network

hyperparameters.dataset_features: 30 PCA-transformed features plus Time and Amount

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical transaction features are encoded into quantum states; amplitude encoding maps normalized feature vectors into amplitudes, while angle encoding maps each feature to a rotation angle on a qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of credit card transactions as fraudulent or legitimate, minimizing classification error / weighted loss in an imbalanced dataset.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Weighted loss function to address class imbalance; hybrid quantum-classical loop with classical optimizer.

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on a European credit card transaction dataset with severe class imbalance.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset (Kaggle / European credit card transactions)

dataset_specification.description: September 2013 transactions; 284,807 records; 492 fraudulent (0.172%); 30 PCA-transformed features (V1-V30) plus Time and Amount; split 70:30 for training/testing.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Imputation of missing values, standardization of numerical features, categorical variable encoding, PCA-transformed features used, normalization before quantum encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single train/test evaluation on a 70:30 split; metrics reported on the 30% test set.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning, missing-value imputation, standardization of numerical features, categorical variable encoding, normalization before quantum encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measurement outputs from the VQC are fed into a classical neural network for final binary classification.

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper suggests potential advantages from quantum superposition and entanglement, but does not provide a measured speedup or formal complexity comparison for this experiment.
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical runtime comparison or asymptotic speedup is reported; advantages are described qualitatively.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not specified; paper provides no qubit count, circuit depth, or scaling analysis required to estimate resources for advantage.
